kurz: With a flat, you acquire a membership that cannot be terminated, the earlier resolutions and a share of the community's renovation backlog; you can read about this in documents that usually have to be requested explicitly.

bloecke.md:
When you buy a flat (Eigentumswohnung), you acquire three things at once: separate ownership (Sondereigentum) of the rooms, a co-ownership share in the common property and a membership of the community of owners that cannot be terminated. As a result of the Apartment Ownership Modernisation Act (Wohnungseigentumsmodernisierungsgesetz), the [[Community of unit owners (Gemeinschaft der Wohnungseigentümer)|community of unit owners (Gemeinschaft der Wohnungseigentümer)]] has been a legal entity in its own right since 1 December 2020 (Section 9a WEG, Apartment Ownership Act). It concludes contracts, holds assets, sues and can be sued. Management lies with the community; the individual owner takes part in it through their vote at the owners' meeting.

The boundary between separate and common property often runs differently from what owners expect. Windows, balcony slabs, the front door of the flat, load-bearing walls, risers and the roof are common property, even if only a single flat uses them or is affected by damage to them. The interior paintwork of a window is separate property, but the frame is not. An owner decides alone on the renovation of their bathroom; the community decides on the waterproofing of their balcony.

## Declaration of division and community rules

The **declaration of division** (Teilungserklärung) divides the property into separate ownership units and assigns co-ownership shares to each unit, usually in thousandths. The attached division plan (Aufteilungsplan) with the certificate of self-containment (Abgeschlossenheitsbescheinigung, Section 7(4) WEG) shows which cellar room and which parking space belong to the flat as property and which are only allocated to it through an exclusive right of use (Sondernutzungsrecht). The difference matters because an exclusive right of use cannot be sold separately and can come with obligations.

The second part, the community rules (Gemeinschaftsordnung), governs the internal relationship between the owners, that is, cost allocation, voting rights, restrictions on use and opening clauses (Öffnungsklauseln). The statutory default is cost allocation according to co-ownership shares (Section 16(2) sentence 1 WEG) and, for voting rights, the per-capita principle (Kopfprinzip), that is, one vote per owner (Section 25(2) WEG). In practice, the community rules often replace the per-capita principle with the value principle (votes according to co-ownership shares) or the unit principle (one vote per unit). Since 2020, the community has been able to change the allocation formula for individual costs or entire types of cost by simple majority (Section 16(2) sentence 2 WEG). This power is far-reaching and can also be used against a minority, for example against the owners of the ground-floor flats with regard to the lift costs.

Resolutions generally bind every later buyer, even if they are not entered in the land register. **Agreements** that deviate from the statutory rules, by contrast, only take effect against a buyer if they are entered in the land register as part of the content of separate ownership. Since 1 December 2020, this has also applied to resolutions adopted on the basis of an opening clause (Section 10(3) sentence 1 WEG). A buyer therefore only finds out which legal position they take on with the flat by reading the resolutions and the registered agreements.

bloecke.md:
## Service charge, budget and annual statement

Since the reform, the owners' meeting only votes on the advance payments resulting from the budget (Wirtschaftsplan) and no longer on the budget as a whole (Section 28(1) WEG). After the end of the year, it accordingly only votes on the balance of the annual statement (Abrechnungsspitze), that is, on additional payments or the adjustment of the ongoing advance payments, and not on the annual statement itself (Section 28(2) WEG). A challenge is therefore directed against the payment amount adopted and not against the figures in the statement.

A low [[Service charge (Hausgeld)|service charge]] is no argument for buying, because as a rule it means that the community sets little aside. For buy-to-let investors, it also matters which part of the service charge can be passed on to the tenant. Operating costs within the meaning of the Operating Costs Ordinance are recoverable; administrative costs and the costs of maintenance and repair are expressly not (Section 1(2) BetrKV). In the illustrative calculation above, the owner bears €92 of the €264 a month personally. That is just over €1,100 a year that is missing from the return calculation if the service charge is treated across the board as a pass-through item.

Since 2020, the property manager has also had to prepare an asset report (Vermögensbericht) and make it available to every owner (Section 28(4) WEG). It states the level of the reserves and the main joint assets. Of all the documents you can request before a purchase, it is the shortest one with meaningful information.

bloecke.titel: Three key figures on the community
bloecke.md: The meaningful figures are the service charge per square metre, the level of the maintenance reserve (Erhaltungsrücklage) per square metre and the total of outstanding service charges of all owners. The first two figures are in the budget and in the asset report; you have to ask for the third. Service charges that individual owners do not pay are ultimately borne by the community.

## Maintenance reserve

Proper management includes building up an appropriate [[Maintenance reserve (Erhaltungsrücklage)|maintenance reserve]] (Section 19(2) no. 4 WEG). The law does not specify what level is appropriate. The official flat rates of the Second Computation Ordinance (Section 28 II. BV) serve as a basis for calculation. Since 1 January 2026, they have been €11.50 per square metre of living space per year for buildings under 22 years old, €14.58 for those aged 22 to 31 years and €18.62 for 32 years and over, with a surcharge if there is a lift. The ordinance sets out initial values from 2002, which have been adjusted to the consumer price index every three years since 2005. These rates apply to the entire building including separate ownership. Usually around two thirds to three quarters of this is attributable to the common property.

The money belongs to the community and not to the individual owner. Nothing is therefore paid out on sale; the share effectively passes to the buyer. This has two tax consequences. The reserve does not reduce the tax base of the real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer; BFH judgment of 16 September 2020, II R 49/17). In addition, a landlord cannot deduct their allocation to the reserve immediately as income-related expenses (Werbungskosten). It is only deductible in the year in which the community spends the money on the maintenance measure.

bloecke.md: Reserves lose value as construction prices rise. The construction price index for residential buildings in May 2026 was 5.0% above the same month of the previous year, and between 2010 and 2025 construction prices for residential buildings rose by around 89%. A reserve that would have been enough for a roof twelve years ago now covers only part of the costs. The community raises the missing amount through a [[Special levy (Sonderumlage)|special levy (Sonderumlage)]]. This is an additional advance payment decided by simple majority.

bloecke.formel: Special levy per unit = (Total costs − Withdrawal from the reserve) × Co-ownership share
bloecke.erklaerung: The same allocation formula applies as for the ongoing service charge, unless the community rules provide otherwise (Section 16(2) WEG).
variablen: Approved costs of the measure including planning and incidental costs
Amount that the owners' meeting releases from the maintenance reserve

bloecke.beispiel: Illustrative calculation: the roof renovation costs €420,000, of which €95,000 is taken from the reserve, leaving €325,000 to be allocated. A flat with 78.5 of 1,000 shares bears €325,000 × 0.0785 = €25,512.50.

bloecke.titel: Special levy on a change of owner
bloecke.md: The special levy is owed by the owner to whom the flat belongs when the respective instalment falls due, regardless of whom it belonged to at the time of the vote. If an amount is approved in March and the second instalment is due in October, it can fall on a buyer who was entered in the land register in August. Every purchase contract should therefore state explicitly who bears the costs of measures that have been approved but not yet called up. Before signing, the buyer should also inspect the register of resolutions (Beschluss-Sammlung). If a seller does not have the minutes “to hand right now”, that is already a finding for the review.

## Owners' meeting and majorities

The owners' meeting takes place at least once a year (Section 24(1) WEG). Invitations are sent in text form with a notice period of at least three weeks (Section 24(4) WEG). Resolutions are adopted by a majority of the votes cast (Section 25(1) WEG). The former quorum of more than half of the co-ownership shares was abolished without replacement on 1 December 2020. A meeting attended by four of twenty-four owners is therefore quorate and also decides on the money of those absent. Owners who neither attend nor grant a proxy leave the decision to those present.

A simple majority is sufficient for maintenance measures. For structural alterations such as a lift, a balcony extension or a photovoltaic system, a simple majority decides whether the measure is carried out, but not who pays for it. All owners bear the costs only if the resolution achieves both more than two thirds of the votes cast and half of all co-ownership shares and the costs are not disproportionate, or if the measure pays for itself within a reasonable time (Section 21(2) WEG). Otherwise, only the owners who voted in favour pay and benefit (Section 21(3) WEG). Irrespective of this, every owner is entitled to be permitted, at their own expense, measures for accessibility, a charging point for an electric vehicle, burglary protection, a fibre-optic connection and, since October 2024, a plug-in solar device (Sections 20(2), 21(1) WEG).

bloecke.titel: Course of a resolution and deadline for challenges
bloecke.unter: After one month, a resolution can practically no longer be challenged, not even by later buyers of the flat.

bloecke.md:
## Property manager and advisory board

The property manager is appointed for at most five years, or for at most three years on the first appointment after the flat ownership has been established (Section 26(2) WEG). The manager can be dismissed at any time and without cause; the manager's contract ends no later than six months after dismissal (Section 26(3) WEG). Since 1 December 2023, every owner can demand the appointment of a certified property manager who has passed an examination before the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (Sections 26a, 19(2) no. 6 WEG). Small communities that manage themselves are exempt.

The advisory board (Verwaltungsbeirat) supports and supervises the property manager (Section 29 WEG). It should examine the budget and the annual statement before the vote and attach an opinion to them. If the members of the advisory board work without pay, they are only liable for intent and gross negligence. This limitation of liability makes it easier to recruit owners for the role.

bloecke.md: First read the minutes of the last five years in chronological order and note every postponed measure. Then consult the asset report and divide the reserve by the total living space of the development. If, for a forty-year-old building, the result is well below what ten years of allocations of the order of magnitude of Section 28 II. BV would have produced, a special levy is certain; only the timing is open. Next, ask the property manager for the total of outstanding service charges and check the management contract for extra fees. Items such as “attendance at meetings” or “preparation of the annual statement” belong in the basic fee.

Owner-occupiers too can claim the labour cost portion of the community's invoices for tradespeople's services that is attributable to their flat. The tax reduction is 20% of the labour costs, at most €1,200 a year (Section 35a(3) EStG, Income Tax Act). The prerequisites are a certificate from the property manager and a non-cash payment (Section 35a(5) EStG). Many property managers provide the breakdown only on request, although it is part of proper management.

Since 29 July 2026, heating has been governed by the Building Modernisation Act (Gebäudemodernisierungsgesetz, GModG), as the Buildings Energy Act (Gebäudeenergiegesetz) has been called since then. The reform abolished the former requirement to operate new heating systems with 65% renewable energy. If a gas or oil heating system is newly installed in an existing building, a rising share of the heat must come from biomethane, bio-oil or certain types of hydrogen from 2029, initially 10% and 60% from 2040 (Section 43 GModG). With central heating, replacement is a matter for the community; the decision is taken at the owners' meeting and not by the individual owner. The investment remains of the same order of magnitude and therefore belongs in the reserve planning.

mitnehmen: With a flat, you acquire at the same time a co-ownership share, a membership that cannot be terminated and the obligation to abide by the resolutions adopted before the purchase.

A low service charge usually means that costs are being postponed; since 2026, the official guide values for total maintenance have been €11.50 to €18.62 per square metre per year (Section 28 II. BV).

Around a third of a typical service charge cannot be passed on to tenants under Section 1(2) BetrKV, and a return calculation that overlooks this shows a net rental yield that is considerably too high.
Since 1 December 2020, there has been no quorum, so four people present can decide for twenty-four owners; after one month, a resolution can practically no longer be challenged (Section 45 WEG).

The maintenance reserve belongs to the community, is not paid out on sale, does not reduce the real estate transfer tax and is deductible by landlords as income-related expenses only when it is spent.

begriffe.begriff: Community of unit owners (Gemeinschaft der Wohnungseigentümer)
begriffe.text: Since 1 December 2020, a legal entity in its own right (Section 9a WEG). It is responsible for management, concludes contracts, holds the joint assets including the maintenance reserve and is a party to court proceedings.

Deed that divides a property into separate ownership units and assigns co-ownership shares to each unit. Its second part, the community rules (Gemeinschaftsordnung), sets out cost allocation, voting rights and rules of use.

Monthly advance payment towards the costs of the community based on the budget (Section 28(1) WEG). It covers operating costs that are recoverable from tenants as well as non-recoverable items such as the property manager's fee and allocations to the reserve.

Savings of the community for the maintenance of the common property (Section 19(2) no. 4 WEG). It is not paid out on sale and is deductible by landlords as income-related expenses only when it is spent.

Register of all resolutions and relevant operative parts of court judgments, with date and wording, which the property manager must keep (Section 24(7) WEG). Every owner may inspect it, prospective buyers only with the seller's authorisation.

Additional advance payment adopted by resolution when the reserve does not cover a measure. It is allocated according to the applicable cost allocation formula and must be paid by the owner who is entered in the land register when it falls due.
